newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil begins to charge financial transaction tax.
newsitem.headline: Brazil begins to charge financial transaction tax.

text.p: A new Brazilian tax of 0.2 percent on financial transactions came into effect today to provide funds for the Health Ministry, officials said.

The Provisional Contribution on Financial Transactions, or CPMF tax, will be in place for one year and is expected to raise some 400 million reais a month to finance health services, though news reports said most of the revenue will be used to pay off debt.

The CPMF tax was approved last year by Congress after heavy lobbying by former Health Minister Adib Jatene, who resigned shortly afterwards due to fallout the tax battle created between him and the government.
Analysts said the new tax is unlikely to pressure Brazil's inflation and primary interest rates, but it is expected to raise costs of bank loans and hurt some types of investment funds.

Short-term funds and Certificates of Deposits (CDBs) are expected to lose investors as the 0.2 percent tax could eliminate most or all of their gains, they said. So far this month, short-term funds have lost 931 million reais of their total 22 billion reais in assets.

On stock investments, foreigners will pay the tax upon opening and closing out their investments on the local bolsas. Domestic and non-Brazilian investors will be exempt from paying the tax on transactions within the bolsas.
